---
title: "Fit a linear model and predict"
---

Fit fuel economy from weight and number of cylinders, then predict two cars with 95% prediction intervals.

The data are [mtcars](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#mtcars): fuel consumption and design of 32 cars (1973–74 models) from *Motor Trend*. `mpg` is miles per US gallon, `wt` is weight in 1,000 lb, and `cyl` is the number of cylinders. The example reads the file by URL with phibble (`composer require phpstats/phibble`) and runs with the phit extension or the plain-PHP polyfill ([Extension or polyfill](../extension-or-polyfill.qmd)).

## Code

```php
use Phibble\DataFrame;

use function Phit\{fit_ols, predict};

$cars = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/mtcars.csv',
);

$fit = fit_ols('mpg ~ wt + factor(cyl)', $cars);

foreach ($fit['columns'] as $i => $name) {
    printf(
        "%-14s %7.2f  95%% CI [%6.2f, %6.2f]\n",
        $name,
        $fit['coefficients'][$i],
        ...$fit['conf_int'][$i],
    );
}
printf(
    "R-squared %.3f, residual SD %.2f\n\n",
    $fit['r_squared'],
    $fit['sigma'],
);

$new = ['wt' => [2.5, 3.5], 'cyl' => [4, 8]];
$p = predict($fit, $new, interval: 'prediction');

foreach ($p['fit'] as $i => $mpg) {
    printf(
        "%5.0f lb, %d cyl %6.2f  95%% PI [%5.2f, %5.2f]\n",
        1000 * $new['wt'][$i],
        $new['cyl'][$i],
        $mpg,
        $p['lower'][$i],
        $p['upper'][$i],
    );
}
```

## Output

```
(Intercept)      33.99  95% CI [ 30.12,  37.86]
wt               -3.21  95% CI [ -4.75,  -1.66]
factor(cyl)6     -4.26  95% CI [ -7.09,  -1.42]
factor(cyl)8     -6.07  95% CI [ -9.46,  -2.69]
R-squared 0.837, residual SD 2.56

 2500 lb, 4 cyl  25.98  95% PI [20.50, 31.46]
 3500 lb, 8 cyl  16.70  95% PI [11.22, 22.18]
```

## Interpretation

- `factor(cyl)` treats the number of cylinders as categories. Four cylinders is the reference, and `factor(cyl)6` and `factor(cyl)8` compare six and eight cylinders with four for cars of the same weight.
- The `wt` coefficient is the difference in miles per gallon associated with 1,000 lb more weight among cars with the same number of cylinders. It describes these 32 cars, not the effect of adding weight to a car.
- With 32 cars and correlated predictors, the intervals are wide.
- A prediction interval covers one new car's mileage. A confidence interval (`interval: 'confidence'`) covers the mean mileage of such cars and is narrower.
